item.title: The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas | Additional Films and Guests — Wed Sep 30, 7:00 PM — IU Cinema
item.description: When a pious television "reporter" Melvin P. Thorpe (Dom DeLuise) threatens to expose Miss Mona's (Dolly Parton) Texas brothel—the Chicken Ranch—to public scandal and close it down for good, she vows not to go down without a fight! With the help of her long-time secret sweetie Sheriff Ed Earl Dodd (Burt Reynolds), the two join together to keep the ranch open and, naturally, deepen their own romance along the way. Sing along through this extraordinary story about passion, scandal, community, and resistance! First premiering as a Broadway musical in 1978, The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas film adaptation was a critical mixed bag upon its release, but the people loved it! The film brought in the biggest weekend box-office opening for a musical up to that point in time and was nominated for two Golden Globes: Best Motion Picture - Musical or Comedy and Best Actress in a Motion Picture or Comedy for Parton. item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Thu Oct 1 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Thu Oct 1 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Thu Oct 1 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers

item.title: Daniel Luis Martinez: The Blueprint | Exhibition — Fri Oct 2 — The Contemporary Art Museum of Indianapolis
item.description: Opening reception: Friday, October 2, 2026, 6–10pm Exhibition on view: October 2–December 18, 2026 For this exhibition, the blueprint is used as both a representational and conceptual departure point. Daniel Luis Martinez uses cyanotype printmaking and mixed-media drawing techniques as a generative process to imagine a speculative home on the CAMi campus. The hybrid drawings and prints featured in the exhibition explore the tactile middle-ground of the blueprint as a creative endeavor. The series employs orthographic conventions typical of architectural drawing sets, though not as precise instructions for building. Rather, a layered and loose approach expresses ideas of home as an architectonic language. Daniel Luis Martinez is a registered architect, educator, and co-founder of the multi-disciplinary design studio LAA Office, which explores the intersection of landscape, art, and architecture. His research and creative work investigate the potential of public art to generate alter

item.title: Kevin & Dianne Brown Students & Alumni Networking Dinner — Fri Oct 2, 5:00 PM — Neal-Marshall Black Culture Center275 N Eagleson Ave. Bloomington
item.description: Keynote Speaker: Kenneth L. Parker '97 — Kenneth L. Parker (https://www.taftlaw.com/people/kenneth-parker/) is a partner at Taft in Cincinnati, where he focuses his practice on compliance, investigations, white collar defense, and commercial litigation. Before joining Taft, Parker spent more than 25 years with the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Ohio, including serving as the presidentially appointed U.S. Attorney from 2021 to 2025. During his tenure, he oversaw a wide range of criminal and civil matters involving public corruption, fraud, national security, cybercrime, civil rights, and other significant legal issues. A 1997 graduate of the Indiana University Maurer School of Law, Parker brings extensive experience in federal law enforcement and the legal profession to this year's Maurer Law community gathering.Event Schedule5 p.m. — Welcome Reception5:45 p.m. — Welcome & Introductions6 p.m. — Keynote Address6:30 p.m. — Dinner7:35 p.m. — Dessert & Alumni Reflection

item.title: Maya, Give Me a Title | Adapt/Construct, CINEkids International Children's Film Series — Sat Oct 3, 4:00 PM — IU CINEMA
item.description:
Maya and her dad—producer and filmmaker Michel Gondry—live in two different countries. In order to stay in touch, her dad asks her every evening, "Maya, give me a title." Based on her answer, he creates a short animated reply in which Maya is the hero. In this charming and clever stop-motion animated adventure, the always innovative and whimsical Gondry brings to life a poetic and amusing journey that will have the little ones dreaming and the grown-ups smiling. [61 min; animation, adventure, family; French with English subtitles]Before the screening, join us at 3pm in our lower lobby for a fun flipbook-making activity! Then, on October 24, come to the IU Sciences Library (located inside the Chemistry Building at 800 E. Kirkwood Ave.) anytime between 10am-4pm for a hands-on investigation into how things move. Show them your IU Cinema flipbook for a special sticker and goodie bag!
Source: IU Bloomington Libraries, IU Cinema, Pillar Arts Community Calendar

item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Mon Oct 5 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Mon Oct 5 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. item.title: Daniel Luis Martinez: The Blueprint | Exhibition — Tue Oct 6 — The Contemporary Art Museum of Indianapolis
item.description: Opening reception: Friday, October 2, 2026, 6–10pm Exhibition on view: October 2–December 18, 2026 For this exhibition, the blueprint is used as both a representational and conceptual departure point. Daniel Luis Martinez uses cyanotype printmaking and mixed-media drawing techniques as a generative process to imagine a speculative home on the CAMi campus. The hybrid drawings and prints featured in the exhibition explore the tactile middle-ground of the blueprint as a creative endeavor. The series employs orthographic conventions typical of architectural drawing sets, though not as precise instructions for building. Rather, a layered and loose approach expresses ideas of home as an architectonic language. Daniel Luis Martinez is a registered architect, educator, and co-founder of the multi-disciplinary design studio LAA Office, which explores the intersection of landscape, art, and architecture. His research and creative work investigate the potential of public art to generate alter

item.description:
Looking for a welcoming space to crochet, knit, embroider, quilt, and explore other fiber arts? Interested in sharing your experiences and connecting with others while learning new skills? Or even just want a place to vent while you work on your scarf you've been crocheting for 2 years? Look no further; join us for Common Threads! Common Threads is a free program open to the public and offers a welcoming environment to share, unwind, and learn! You can bring your own fiber art to work on while working alongside others who enjoy working in fiber and textiles. Or you can try learning something new; we welcome all skill levels! Either way, you're sure to have a good time. This group meets on the 1st and 3rd Tuesday of each month from 3–4:30 p.m., excluding holidays and museum closures.
